question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Twin-cell split assay with lineage barcodes to measure the memory half-life
ideas.description: Barcode cells, deliver a brief AP-1-activating stimulus, then let clones divide and physically split sister/cousin cells so one is profiled (scRNA-seq or reporter level) while the relative is challenged later. The concordance between relatives as a function of elapsed generations gives a quantitative memory half-life in divisions, and distinguishes true heritable memory from slowly decaying protein that is diluted equally in all cells.

ideas.title: Degron time-window dissection of writing, maintaining, and reading
ideas.description: Use dTAG or auxin degrons on endogenously tagged FOS and JUN to remove AP-1 protein only during the stimulus, only during the quiescent interval, or only at the time of the second challenge. If memory survives depletion during the interval but not during the stimulus, the information is stored in something AP-1 deposits rather than in AP-1 itself.

ideas.title: Post-replication single-molecule footprinting of AP-1 enhancers
ideas.description: Combine nascent-strand labeling with single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) to ask whether AP-1 motifs on newly replicated daughter chromatin are re-opened and co-occupied in cis, and how fast. This tests the central requirement for epigenetic memory, that the state is re-established on both daughter molecules after each round of replication.

ideas.title: Two-pulse potentiation kinetics and information-theoretic memory capacity
ideas.description: Deliver pairs of stimulus pulses with systematically varied inter-pulse intervals and read out single-cell AP-1 target induction, fitting the decay of potentiation to get a memory time constant. Computing the mutual information between past stimulus history and the current single-cell state quantifies how many bits of history AP-1 actually stores, and whether memory is graded or bistable.

ideas.title: Synthetic enhancer library screen for memory-competent AP-1 grammar
ideas.description: Build a reporter library systematically varying AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, and flanking partner motifs, integrate it at a fixed locus, and sort for reporters that stay on long after the stimulus ends. This converts a correlative question into a sufficiency test and reveals which cis-architectures are necessary to convert a transient AP-1 input into a persistent state.

candidates: Lineage barcoding (e.g. Watermelon/CellTag) with a transient AP-1 stimulus, then measure how many divisions the induced state remains clonally concordant
Twin/sister-cell split assay: separate sisters, profile one and challenge the other, to test whether AP-1 state predicts a relative's future response
Long-term live imaging of an endogenous FOS/JUN fluorescent knock-in to measure mother-daughter correlation decay across pedigrees
Auxin/dTAG degron depletion of FOS or JUN restricted to defined time windows to separate writing, maintaining, and reading of memory
CUT&RUN time course after a brief stimulus to test whether AP-1 occupancy outlives AP-1-driven transcription
ATAC-seq hysteresis test: does AP-1-opened enhancer accessibility persist after the factor is acutely removed
Single-molecule chromatin fiber footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) to see whether AP-1 sites remain co-occupied in cis on individual molecules
Replication-coupled accessibility (Repli-ATAC/scsNOMe) to ask whether AP-1 sites are re-opened on nascent daughter strands
Live imaging and mitotic CUT&RUN to test mitotic bookmarking by AP-1 on condensed chromosomes
Stimulus dose ramp up and down to test for bistability/hysteresis in AP-1 reporter activity
Synthetic AP-1 reporter with autoregulatory feedback deleted, to test whether positive feedback is necessary for persistence
Two-pulse potentiation assay varying inter-pulse interval to extract a quantitative memory decay constant
Block new protein synthesis or new transcription during the interval to distinguish protein-based from chromatin-based memory
Optogenetic AP-1 (LOV-Fos) to decouple amplitude, duration, and frequency of input from the persistence of output
CRISPRi of individual AP-1 family members only during the maintenance phase to find the carrier of memory
Endogenous tagging plus FRAP/SPT to compare AP-1 protein half-life and residence time with the memory timescale
Compare memory retention in cell-cycle-arrested versus cycling cells to separate division-coupled dilution from time-based decay
Allele-specific AP-1 occupancy and expression to test whether memory is transmitted in cis or in trans
Cross-stimulus transfer test: does AP-1 memory from stimulus A alter the response to an unrelated stimulus B
Information-theoretic analysis of mutual information between stimulus history and current single-cell AP-1 state
Massively parallel reporter library varying AP-1 motif number, affinity, and spacing to find architectures that sustain memory
Proteomic interactome of AP-1 at early versus late times to identify maintenance cofactors
In vivo re-injury experiment in AP-1 reporter mice to test wound-healing memory
Prospective sorting on an AP-1 reporter followed by relaxation and re-sorting to measure state interconversion rates
Single-cell multiome before and after restimulation to test whether primed cells respond faster and larger
